_comment: The 4-cell preprocessing ablation for the TF-IDF + logistic-regression control.
Two axes: whether the conventional hygiene chain (alphanumeric-only filter, NLTK
stopword removal, Porter stemming) is applied, and whether the vectorizer can see
bigrams. The chain deletes negation -- 'not', 'no' and 'nor' are NLTK English
stopwords, and the ^\w+$ filter destroys "n't" before the stopword filter runs --
so with unigrams only, 'not good' and 'good' collapse to the same feature vector.
Run with: uv run python train.py -c cfg/small.yaml -p cfg/baseline_ablation.json --baselines-only

cells.label: notebook chain, uni+bigram
cells.note: bigrams cannot recover tokens the chain already deleted
